mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 2100 units signals increased consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence indices
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 55% of instances when HOUST > 2100, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 3.5% eases borrowing costs, boosting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 3.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 in a month, the combined signal predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and SPX correlation
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of instances when the labor market trigger is met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 5% YoY signals increased economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 52% of instances when INDPRO YoY growth > 5%, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real disposable personal income (RSAFS) growth below -2% YoY indicates decreased consumer spending power, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical RSAFS and consumer spending correlation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 55% of instances when RSAFS YoY growth < -2%, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive 3-month declines in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPI (CPIAUCSL) signal a monetary easing cycle with controlled inflation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month consecutive declines in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL
regime_hint: monetary easing cycle with low inflation
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 48% of instances when the dual decline trigger is met, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth, as a standalone indicator, predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to its historically strong correlation with economic activity.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.035 over any 2-year rolling window, or PAYEMS growth does not significantly correlate with 20-day forward SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: GDP (GDPC1) growth above 4% YoY, combined with a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4%), signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of instances when the dual growth trigger is met, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.
